title: Speculative Layer Supertypes (The Abstract Layer Castle)
pattern: Defining a deep, rigid hierarchy of abstract layer supertypes or marker traits representing theoretical meta-categories (e.g., `IdentifiedValueObject`) that concrete types must inherit or implement.
why_bad:
*   **Cognitive Load:** Developers must understand multiple layers of meta-abstractions before they can write a simple data holder or value.
*   **Rigidity:** It forces an upfront design architecture that does not easily adapt as the team's understanding of the domain shifts.
detection: Trait or class hierarchies with $\ge 3$ levels of nesting where the top-level items are behaviorless marker classes containing only ID fields.
counterexample: **Standard Compiler-Checked Traits:** Blanket trait implementations enforced by the compiler (e.g., `Send + Sync + Clone`) are valid.
source: Vernon, *Implementing Domain-Driven Design*, Chapter 6 "Value Objects" (Layer Supertypes) & McConnell, *Code Complete*, Section 24.2.
